resources.string: Blood enters the right atrium from the body and the left atrium from the lungs. The tricuspid and mitral valves open and the ventricles fill.
The atria finish filling the ventricles
Both atria squeeze, pushing the last part of the filling volume through the open inlet valves.
The inlet valves close. Pressure rises before the outlet valves open, so blood is not yet ejected and ventricular volume stays nearly constant.
The pulmonary valve opens toward the lungs, and the aortic valve opens toward the body. The ventricles narrow as blood leaves.
The outlet valves close. Pressure drops while all four valves are closed, until the next filling phase begins.
Slowed teaching animation. Colored arrows indicate relative oxygen content and flow direction, not the actual color of blood. Not a measurement of your heart.
Source: blood flow through the heart (NIH)
